quick: With or without food; bedtime if sedating
Use only if clearly needed; weigh risk
summary: Doxepin is a tricyclic antidepressant used for depression and/or anxiety, including those associated with organic disease or alcoholism. Usual adult dose is 75-150 mg/day, up to 300 mg/day in severe illness. It carries a boxed warning for increased suicidality in children, adolescents and young adults. Anticholinergic effects, sedation and cardiac conduction effects are characteristic; overdose can be fatal. Low-dose formulations (3-6 mg) are used separately for insomnia.
indications: Psychoneurotic patients with depression and/or anxiety
Depression and/or anxiety associated with alcoholism (not taken with alcohol)
Depression and/or anxiety associated with organic disease
Psychotic depressive disorders with associated anxiety, including involutional depression and manic-depressive disorders
Low-dose (3-6 mg) formulation: insomnia characterized by difficulty with sleep maintenance

dosage.t: Once daily at bedtime or divided
dosage.n: Doses up to 150 mg may be given as a single bedtime dose

dosage.d: Start low (e.g., 25-50 mg/day) and titrate slowly
dosage.n: Greater sensitivity to anticholinergic and cardiac effects

admin: Take orally; the capsule liquid concentrate should be diluted in water/juice before use (not grape juice or carbonated beverages)
A sedating dose may be given at bedtime to aid sleep and adherence
Titrate gradually based on response and tolerability
Allow at least 2-3 weeks for antidepressant effect
Do not stop abruptly; taper to avoid discontinuation symptoms
moa: Doxepin is a tricyclic antidepressant that inhibits reuptake of norepinephrine and serotonin at the presynaptic neuron, increasing their synaptic availability. It is also a potent antagonist at histamine H1 (sedation, antipruritic effect), muscarinic acetylcholine (anticholinergic effects) and alpha-1 adrenergic receptors (orthostatic hypotension). Membrane-stabilizing (quinidine-like) effects underlie its cardiac conduction toxicity in overdose.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to doxepin or other dibenzoxepines
Concurrent use with or within 14 days of an MAO inhibitor
relative: Cardiovascular disease, conduction abnormalities or recent myocardial infarction
Benign prostatic hyperplasia / bladder outlet obstruction
monitor: History of suicidality or young adults (boxed warning)
Concomitant CNS depressants, anticholinergics or QT-prolonging drugs

preg: Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus. Neonates exposed to TCAs in the third trimester may have withdrawal/adaptation symptoms; weigh maternal benefit against risk.
lact: Doxepin and its active metabolite are excreted in breast milk; cases of infant sedation and respiratory depression have been reported. Breastfeeding is not recommended during doxepin therapy.
renal: Use with caution; start at a low dose and titrate slowly because reduced clearance can increase levels and anticholinergic/cardiac effects.
hepatic: Doxepin undergoes extensive hepatic metabolism (CYP2D6/2C19); use with caution in hepatic impairment with lower starting doses and slow titration.

major: MAO inhibitors - risk of hyperpyretic crisis, severe convulsions and serotonin syndrome; do not use within 14 days
Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors (fluoxetine, paroxetine, quinidine) - markedly increase doxepin levels and toxicity
Other CNS depressants/alcohol - additive sedation and respiratory depression
Drugs prolonging QT (Class I/III antiarrhythmics) - additive arrhythmia risk
moderate: Anticholinergic drugs - additive anticholinergic toxicity (ileus, urinary retention, delirium)
minor: Oral contraceptives / estrogens - may alter TCA levels and effect
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; dilute oral concentrate in water/juice, not carbonated drinks.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol - additive CNS and respiratory depression and increased overdose lethality.
interactions.diagnostics: Can prolong QRS/QT on ECG; may interfere with some urine catecholamine assays.

emergency: Cardiac dysrhythmia / severe hypotension in overdose
Serotonin syndrome or hyperpyretic crisis with MAOIs

monitoring: Mood, behavior and emergence of suicidality, especially early and at dose changes (boxed warning)
Baseline and periodic ECG in patients with cardiac risk or higher doses
Anticholinergic effects (bowel/bladder function, confusion, especially elderly)
counsel: Effect on mood may take 2-3 weeks; keep taking as prescribed and do not stop suddenly
Watch for and report worsening mood, agitation or thoughts of self-harm, especially early in treatment
Avoid alcohol and other sedating drugs; it may cause drowsiness - use caution driving
Rise slowly to avoid dizziness; report fast/irregular heartbeat, fainting or trouble urinating
Dilute the oral concentrate in water or juice (not carbonated beverages) just before taking
pk: Antidepressant effect over 2-3 weeks; sedation rapid
Supports once-daily bedtime dosing for many patients
Store at controlled room temperature, protected from light
pearls: Boxed warning: increased risk of suicidal thinking and behavior in children, adolescents and young adults - monitor closely
TCA overdose is highly lethal (cardiac dysrhythmia, seizures, coma) - manage in hospital and consult poison control
Strongly antihistaminic - useful for antipruritic and hypnotic effects; low-dose (3-6 mg) is approved for insomnia
Do not combine with MAOIs; allow a 14-day washout
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip it and resume the regular schedule; do not double up. For once-daily bedtime dosing, skip a daytime-remembered missed dose if it would cause excess sedation.
overdose: TCA overdose can be fatal. Critical manifestations include cardiac dysrhythmias, severe hypotension, seizures and CNS depression/coma; ECG (QRS/QT) changes guide severity. Provide hospital monitoring, airway/cardiorespiratory support, activated charcoal if early, sodium bicarbonate for cardiotoxicity/QRS widening, and seizure control. Contact a poison control center.
